findings.claim: The commit claims to be docs-only with Risk: none, but it changes runtime ordering in List by adding an id tiebreaker (out[i].ID < out[j].ID) when base key and part number are equal. Previously equal rows compared as equal and, with an unstable sort.Slice, their order was undefined; now it is deterministic. This is a behavior change not disclosed in the commit message. Also, the sort comparator code before the hunk is not visible, so the claimed sibling-key ordering (doc/big, doc/big/part-2, doc/big-x) cannot be confirmed from the diff alone; the new test relies on existing code to satisfy it.
The help text wrapping leaves an orphan line ('is recorded; a') that breaks the column layout of the usage block, reducing readability of the help output.

evidence: The diff changes the comparator in internal/memory/list.go to add an ID tiebreaker, which is a runtime change under a commit labelled docs with Risk: none.
The sort's earlier lines (computing base key bi/bj and part numbers ni/nj) are outside the diff, so the sibling-key ordering is only verified by the new test, not by visible code.
The cli.go usage text rewrap leaves a short dangling line 'is recorded; a'.
